traceability.evidence:
1) Story under assessment - Story file: docs/stories/022.0-DEV-JSDOC-COEXISTENCE.story.md (provided in prompt) - Focus: correct coexistence of traceability annotations (@story, @req, @supports) with other JSDoc tags, proper termination/boundary detection, continuation rules, no false positives, preserved multiline behavior, documentation, and tests.
2) Tests directly tied to this story - Test suite: tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts - From prior inspection (still applicable and consistent with current output), the file header includes traceability back to this story: /** * @story docs/stories/022.0-DEV-JSDOC-COEXISTENCE.story.md * @req REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE * @req REQ-ANNOTATION-TERMINATION * @req REQ-JSDOC-BOUNDARY-DETECTION * @req REQ-CONTINUATION-LOGIC * @req REQ-NO-FALSE-POSITIVES * @req REQ-PRESERVE-MULTILINE */ - Current Jest verbose run (npm test -- --verbose) executed in this assessment shows this suite and the relevant tests passing: "Valid Annotation Format Rule (Story 005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION)" -> valid-annotation-format valid cases include: - ✓ [REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE] traceability before other JSDoc tags - ✓ [REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE] traceability after other JSDoc tags - ✓ [REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE] mixed positions of traceability and other JSDoc tags - ✓ [REQ-PRESERVE-MULTILINE] multi-line @story annotation before other JSDoc tags - ✓ [REQ-NO-FALSE-POSITIVES] JSDoc tags do not pollute requirement ID when following @req - These tests explicitly reference the requirement IDs from this story and validate the specified behaviors.
3) Overall test run - Command: npm test -- --verbose - Result: exit code 0 - Summary from this run: - Test Suites: 40 passed, 40 total - Tests: 302 passed, 302 total - Includes all suites that rely on annotation parsing (valid-annotation-format, valid-story-reference, valid-req-reference, maintenance tools, etc.), indicating no regressions.
4) Implementation behavior (from earlier validated inspection, still supported by current tests) - Core parsing/building logic is in the valid-annotation-format rule internals: - normalizeCommentLine: - Strips leading `*` and whitespace from JSDoc lines but preserves line boundaries and does NOT collapse multiple JSDoc lines into a single string. - Ensures traceability tag lines stay distinct from following JSDoc tags, removing the original bug where newlines were effectively stripped out and tags concatenated. - isNonTraceabilityJSDocTagLine: - Matches lines that start with a JSDoc tag `@word` other than @story, @req, or @supports using a regex like `/^\s*@(?!(story|req|supports)\b)\w+/` (exact code name from prior inspection). - Used as a boundary detector: when a pending traceability annotation exists and a non-traceability JSDoc tag line is seen, the current annotation is finalized and the tag line is not appended. - This directly implements REQ-JSDOC-BOUNDARY-DETECTION and contributes to REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE and REQ-ANNOTATION-TERMINATION. - processCommentLine (and surrounding helpers): - When encountering @story/@req/@supports lines, start/continue a pending annotation value. - Continuation only occurs when the next line does NOT start with any JSDoc tag (per isNonTraceabilityJSDocTagLine and traceability-tag detection). That satisfies REQ-CONTINUATION-LOGIC and REQ-PRESERVE-MULTILINE. - When a boundary JSDoc tag is detected, the current annotation is finalized so later tags are not concatenated into the value (fixing the REQ-OPTIMIZATION@param{object}data bug scenario).
5) Mapping to acceptance criteria - Before Other Tags: - Test: "[REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE] traceability before other JSDoc tags" (valid case) passes. - Confirms annotations work when placed before @param/@returns/etc.
- After Other Tags: - Test: "[REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE] traceability after other JSDoc tags" passes. - Confirms annotations work when placed after other JSDoc tags.
- Mixed Positions: - Test: "[REQ-JSDOC-TAG-COEXISTENCE] mixed positions of traceability and other JSDoc tags" passes. - Confirms interleaved @story/@req and @param/@returns are handled correctly.
- Proper Termination: - Test: "[REQ-NO-FALSE-POSITIVES] JSDoc tags do not pollute requirement ID when following @req" passes. - This is effectively the reproduction of Issue #3; passing indicates annotation values are terminated correctly at the JSDoc boundary (REQ-ANNOTATION-TERMINATION).
- JSDoc Tag Detection: - Implemented by isNonTraceabilityJSDocTagLine, which treats any @word (other than @story/@req/@supports) as a JSDoc boundary. - Verified indirectly through the coexistence/mixed-position tests, satisfying REQ-JSDOC-BOUNDARY-DETECTION.
- Continuation Lines & Preserve Multiline: - Test: "[REQ-PRESERVE-MULTILINE] multi-line @story annotation before other JSDoc tags" passes. - Combined with continuation logic that only extends values when lines do not start with @tag, this fulfills REQ-CONTINUATION-LOGIC and REQ-PRESERVE-MULTILINE.
- Error Messages / No False Positives: - All coexistence-related tests are in the "valid" group and pass, demonstrating that correctly formatted annotations in any JSDoc position do not raise errors (REQ-NO-FALSE-POSITIVES). - The broader valid-annotation-format suite continues to report errors only for genuine format problems (invalid paths, invalid IDs, malformed @supports), ensuring clear, appropriate error messages when there truly is a problem.
- Backward Compatible: - The full Jest run (40 suites, 302 tests all passing) covers many stories and features depending on annotation parsing. - No other tests failed, indicating the new behavior did not break existing valid annotations or other traceability rules.
- Documentation: - docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md (inspected in the previous assessment and unchanged since) contains a section describing JSDoc coexistence: - Explains that traceability annotations may appear before, after, or mixed with other JSDoc tags. - States that any non-traceability @tag line is treated as a boundary and that continuation lines only apply when a line is not a new @tag. - Includes examples closely matching the story’s suggested cases (traceability before tags, after tags, mixed, and a multiline @story value before @param). - This fulfills the Documentation acceptance criterion.
6) Definition of Done alignment - All acceptance criteria in the story are covered by a combination of: - Passing tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts (tagged with this story’s requirements) and - Updated documentation in docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md. - Current `npm test -- --verbose` run confirms the tests are still passing. - No regressions observed elsewhere in the suite, supporting the "no regressions" and "backward compatible" requirements.
Given this evidence, story 022.0-DEV-JSDOC-COEXISTENCE is fully implemented and currently passing all associated tests.
